assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns a biological process, ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis, into a designable chemical reaction: a heterobifunctional molecule or glue induces proximity between a target and an E3 ligase. It gave biologists a general tool, drugging proteins that lack active sites, and gave medicine a new modality. The mechanism is chemically well defined.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept (2001) and Crews built the field and its clinical translation; Ciulli supplied structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex mechanism. Handa, Ito, Kim and Sakamoto make the glue/thalidomide-cereblon strand and the early PROTAC credit contested, so the three-person configuration omits meaningful contributors.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups, with degraders in clinical trials and cereblon/DDB1 mechanisms confirmed structurally. Recognition is timely, though clinical benefit is still being established.
uncertainties: PROTACs and molecular glues are arguably two discoveries needing separate credit; the ideal trio is not clear.
I rely on recalled knowledge of clinical-stage status and have not verified current trial outcomes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors are a chemical solution to genome editing: engineered deaminases convert one base to another without double-strand breaks, a rare case where enzyme chemistry (cytidine and evolved adenine deamination) was turned into a programmable tool. Impact on research and therapy is large and the underlying chemistry is clear.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the intellectual leader; Komor (CBE) and Gaudelli (ABE) carried out the decisive work as trainees. Nishida and Kondo made an independent cytidine-deaminase-based approach in 2016. A Liu-only prize would also be defensible and CRISPR credit was recognised in 2020.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently, with the first base-editing therapies in the clinic. It is recent (2016 to 2017), so some caution about timing is warranted, and safety data, off-target deamination and long-term outcomes remain open.
uncertainties: The chemistry-versus-biology boundary and the overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize may lead to a Medicine-style argument.
Whether Nishida/Kondo deserve inclusion over a trainee is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aaRS/tRNA pairs that incorporate unnatural amino acids in vivo make protein chemistry programmable, enabling mechanistic enzymology, labelling, photocrosslinking and protein therapeutics. It is a general tool built from a deep understanding of translation chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the in vivo approach and the first E. coli and yeast systems; Chin extended it to eukaryotes and multicellular organisms and to quadruplet decoding and genome recoding. Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama are important but a three-person limit restricts credit. Schultz and Chin are the cleanest pair.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted across laboratories for over twenty years with robust confirmation. Mature and timely, although it has been repeatedly nominated, and the interpretation of efficiency and fidelity is still improving.
uncertainties: Roles of Wang (early work with Schultz), Mehl and Yokoyama complicate the allocation.
Yield and fidelity limits for multi-site incorporation remain a practical limitation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminator chemistry and single-molecule/cluster amplification transformed genomics and medicine and brought down the cost of sequencing by orders of magnitude. The chemistry of the nucleotide analogue, polymerase and cleavable linker is central, which makes it of interest to me for nucleic acid biochemistry.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded Solexa chemistry; Mayer (Manteia clusters), Ju (reversible terminators) and Rothberg (pyrosequencing/ion semiconductor, 454) have parallel claims. Credit across competing platforms is not cleanly separable.
assessment.maturity: Mature and thoroughly validated. Recognition is arguably overdue in impact terms, though the prize may be seen as belonging to Medicine or Physiology.
uncertainties: Competing platform lineages make a fair three-person set hard.
Whether the committee would consider this chemistry rather than biotechnology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometric proteomics, with shotgun sequencing, quantification and data-dependent analysis, made proteome-wide measurement of protein abundance and modification routine. I value it as a measurement method that replaced assumptions with data in biochemistry and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution, quantitative and SILAC-based work), Aebersold (targeted and quantitative, SRM/ICAT) and Yates (shotgun and database search) are the principal figures. Hunt, Gygi and Heck are also strong, and the list is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and widely reproduced, though the prize for ionisation (2002) already recognised the core enabling technology.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize may reduce novelty.
Three-person selection is arbitrary among at least six strong contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Covalent targeting of mutant KRAS G12C and chemical-genetic analogue-sensitive kinases opened an undruggable target and gave a clear chemical mechanism, with a drug (sotorasib) approved. The work links reactivity of a cysteine to selectivity, a clear chemistry-to-medicine story.
assessment.attribution: Shokat is the decisive originator of both strands, so a sole prize is credible, though the covalent KRAS programme drew on Tethering (Wells) and later work by Amgen and Mirati groups.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated and independently reproduced; timing is recent but compelling. Durability of response and resistance mechanisms still evolving.
uncertainties: Two discoveries (chemical genetics and KRAS) are combined and may need different recognition.
The role of Tethering and industrial teams in the clinical molecule is not fully clear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry for siRNA and mRNA medicines, evidenced by the COVID-19 vaccines and patisiran. The key physical-chemical insight is pH-dependent charge for encapsulation and endosomal escape.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and Hope developed the formulation and ionizable lipid concepts (with Madden, MacLachlan); Anderson and Langer contributed lipidoids and combinatorial design. Attribution is tangled across academia and industry and patent disputes.
assessment.maturity: Large and proven impact but the fundamental interpretation of delivery and endosomal escape is still debated. The 2023 Medicine prize recognised the nucleoside modification part rather than delivery.
uncertainties: Entangled credit and patent disputes among several groups.
Mechanistic understanding of endosomal escape is incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible m6A methylation, with writers, erasers and readers, established a regulatory layer of RNA chemistry affecting stability, translation and development. It connects a defined chemical modification to broad biology and disease.
assessment.attribution: He identified FTO as an m6A demethylase and framed the reversible system; Jaffrey (m6A mapping, m6Am) and Rechavi and Dominissini (first transcriptome-wide maps, 2012) contributed key tools. Meyer, Jia and Yang also have claims, and the allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: Replicated broadly, but there are real controversies about the mapping methods and antibody specificity, and the interpretation of some functions is still moving. A measurement-sceptic view suggests waiting.
uncertainties: Quantitative stoichiometry and site-level accuracy of mapping are disputed.
Whether biological function claims are fully robust.
